question.worked_solution:
We can use either of the following two methods.

**Method 1 - The Long Way**

First, remember that a fraction represents a division:

$$
\frac{(\frac{7}{4})}{7}=\frac{7}{4}÷7
$$

Now, recall that dividing by $7$ is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal $\frac{1}{7}.$ We can use this fact to simplify the fraction above:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{4}÷7 & = \\ \frac{7}{4}\times \frac{1}{7} & = \\ \frac{7\times 1}{4\times 7} & = \\ \frac{7}{28}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we simplify:

$$
\frac{7}{28}=\frac{7÷7}{28÷7}=\frac{1}{4}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\frac{(\frac{7}{4})}{7}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

**Method 2 - The Quick Way**

The result will have the same numerator as the top fraction, and the denominator is just the product of the two denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(\frac{7}{4})}{7} & = \\ \frac{7}{4\times 7} & = \\ \frac{7}{28} & = \\ \frac{7÷7}{28÷7} & = \\ \frac{1}{4} & \end{aligned}
$$
